# S292 — Spec check: a sibling project's tracking write in the same git repo must not fail the read-only check

*Proposed.* The spec check fingerprints the main checkout with `git status --porcelain` for the whole repository. So when two ork projects share one repo, a write by the other project fails this project's spec check as "spec-check changed the tree, and it is a read-only role". This slice limits the fingerprint to paths under the project's own root. Whether the project's own `.slicer/` tracking files are left out too, and whether the spec check also takes a lock, are open: see `Open owner questions`.

**Findings:** Owner 2026-11-04: prism and prism-ui are ork projects in one git repo; ork wave start prism S63 failed with 'spec-check changed the tree, and it is a read-only role' while ork wave start prism-ui U34 wrote prism-ui/.slicer in the shared checkout; a retry passed. gitStatusAt (speccheck.go:84-90) fingerprints the whole repository. · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**2026-11-04** — Owner answers 2026-11-04 (interactive): all recommendations accepted as written. Q1 project-only: fingerprint every path under the project root, its own .slicer included. Q2 no-lock: scope the paths only; the spec check takes no lock.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** the read-only fingerprint of roles in a worktree (`treeStatus`, `internal/engine/round.go:101`; a worktree is not the shared main checkout); the landing's dirty-main checks (S254, S217) and its tracking-only merge conflicts (S289); the spec check's shape retry (S266); dropping the fingerprint (adj 28, `role.readonly-fingerprint`, decided yes).

## Why

Owner evidence, 2026-11-04: two ork projects share the git repository at `/Users/jon/code/platforms`, and one branch: prism (`libraries/prism`) and prism-ui (`libraries/prism-ui`). Both are registered in ork's registry with those paths. `ork wave start prism S63 ... --yes` failed with "ork: spec check failed: spec-check changed the tree, and it is a read-only role". This came right after `ork wave start prism-ui U34 ... --yes` had started; its setup wrote prism-ui's `.slicer` tracking files in the shared main checkout while prism's spec check ran. An immediate retry succeeded. (The owner reported the timeline; ork's logs of it were not read.)

What the code at HEAD of main shows (read 2026-11-04):

- `gitStatusAt` (`internal/engine/speccheck.go:84-90`) runs `git -C DIR status --porcelain` with no pathspec. For a project in a subdirectory, that is the whole repository's status.
- `runSpecCheckOnce` takes `baseline` before reading the specs (`internal/engine/speccheck.go:186`), `before` just before the role (`:217`), and `after` once the role ends (`:269`). `baseline != before` returns `errSpecStatusChanged` (`:220-222`). `RunSpecCheck` retries that once (`:148`), which `TestSpecCheckRetriesStatusChangesOutsideTheRole` (`internal/engine/speccheck_test.go:575`) covers. `after != before` returns the hard error "spec-check changed the tree, and it is a read-only role" (`:287-289`). That error is not in the retry set, so a sibling's write during the role fails the whole launch.
- The fingerprint compares porcelain text, so a further edit to a file that was already modified does not change it. Only a status change does: a clean file becoming modified, or a new untracked file. `TestSpecCheckOnADirtyButUnchangedTreeIsFine` (`internal/engine/speccheck_test.go:172`) relies on this. Not verified: this is probably why the spec check's own relay-ledger writes (`d.Slicer.RelayStep` on `root`, `internal/engine/speccheck.go:236` and `:264`, between `before` and `after`) do not trip it: `RelayBegin` (`:131`) has already dirtied the log before `baseline`.
- The landing lock is keyed by project path (`Landings.Acquire(ctx, key)`, `internal/engine/landlock.go:32`; called with `e.proj.Path`, `internal/engine/land.go:35`). The spec check takes no lock. So prism and prism-ui never exclude each other.

Relation to S254 and S217 (dirty main): all three ask which paths in the shared main checkout belong to this project. S254's spec matches tracking paths as `.slicer/`, while `git status --porcelain` and `git diff --name-only` print repo-root paths (`libraries/prism-ui/.slicer/...`). So S254 as written does not see a subdirectory project's tracking files (see the 2026-11-04 note on S254). The fix is shared in one helper only: `projectPrefix(ctx, root) (string, error)` from `git -C root rev-parse --show-prefix`, plus a pathspec of `.` from `-C root`. This slice adds it, and S254 and S217 reuse it. The decisions differ. Here a sibling's write is ignored. In S254 and S217 a dirty path is acted on or warned about.

## Open owner questions

adj 28 (`role.readonly-fingerprint`) keeps the fingerprint; these questions only scope it.

Question: Should the spec check's fingerprint also leave out the project's own .slicer tracking files?
Options:
1. project-only: fingerprint every path under the project root, its .slicer included
2. skip-own-tracking: also exclude the project's own .slicer, since ork, slicer and owner sessions write there during a check
3. scope-and-retry: keep option 1 and treat a change confined to .slicer as a status change outside the role, which gets the existing one retry
Recommend: 1 - it fixes the reported sibling case with the least change; the spec-check role runs in plan mode and cannot write tracking files itself, so add option 2 or 3 only if an own-project write is seen

Question: Should the spec check also take a lock so sibling writes cannot overlap it?
Options:
1. no-lock: scope the paths only
2. repo-lock: a lock keyed by the git top level, which the spec check and every main-checkout tracking write of ork take
3. project-lock: the spec check takes the project's existing landing lock, keyed by project path
Recommend: 1 - a lock would not cover owner sessions or slicer writes outside ork, and option 3 does not cover a sibling project, because the landing lock is keyed by project path
